answer: The per-epoch writing challenge is a concrete sybil brake: every identity must submit fresh prose that a random panel of established peers must attest, and duplicates are rejected on-ledger. A prism splits one beam into many angles, so an attacker needs a distinct original voice for each fake identity, plus the time to answer before each dawn closes the epoch. A single shared pulse of automation betrays itself through near-identical phrasing, so graders withhold attestation and unattested work earns nothing. Cost scales with N texts and N reviews, not one script.
